stops.note: Adolphe Sax was born in 1814 at Dinant in Belgium, son of an instrument maker
Sax + Greek phōnē 'voice, sound'; he patented the instrument in Paris in 1846
first a military-band instrument, it became the voice of jazz from the 1920s through players like Coleman Hawkins and later Charlie Parker

current_meaning: a brass wind instrument with a single reed, common in jazz
